title: D3-3a N05: Minimum Contract and Energy-Margin Pressure Setpoints with a PX
question_prompt:
D3-3a N05: Minimum Contract and Energy-Margin Pressure Setpoints with a PX

With stable seawater quality, operators want to lower pressure without sacrificing capacity. Hold flow, membrane area and PX efficiency fixed; vary only p1_pressure_bar. Find the minimum basic pressure meeting product≥11,000 m³/d and SEC≤3.00 kWh/m³, and the minimum recommended pressure meeting product≥11,200 m³/d and SEC≤3.00 kWh/m³; prove both with adjacent 0.1-bar points. Estimate ERD inlet pressure as P1 outlet minus 2.7 bar and use a 1.0-bar low-pressure outlet. Report available/equivalent recovered brine power, P1/P2 and net power at both limits, and explain why raising pressure increases both production and brine differential pressure but does not necessarily lower SEC.

Feed TDS | 36.5 | g/L | Fixed | Criterion 2 | Product≥11,200 and SEC≤3.00 | 0.1 bar
Feed TSS | 0.03 | g/L | Fixed | Decision variable | P1 outlet pressure | Vary this only
Temperature | 24 | °C | Fixed | Objective | Minimize pressure setpoint | Adjacent proof
Active RO area | 14400 | m² | Fixed
P1 outlet pressure | 69 | bar(a) | Decision variable | Required deliverables
P1 efficiency | 0.82 | - | Fixed | 1. Establish a coarse bracket and control direction.
PX efficiency | 0.95 | - | Fixed | 2. Prove both adjacent limits or both sides of the diagnostic window.
P2 efficiency | 0.82 | - | Fixed | 3. Report key simulate_swro_system outputs.
ERD-inlet loss from P1 | 2.7 | bar | Benchmark audit assumption | 4. Calculate brine flow, available pressure power and equivalent recovered power from product flow.
ERD low-pressure outlet | 1 | bar(a) | Benchmark audit assumption | 5. Distinguish pump-train power, net plant power and the engineering decision.
Operating days | 330 | d/y | Energy conversion

Scope: use simulate_swro_system for whole-plant energy. Available brine power is P=Qbrine×ΔP; equivalent recovered power is ηPX×P for an energy audit. It is not PX shaft power and is not one-for-one with the SEC change. All limits are benchmark rules, not universal standards.
